title: Tooth decay
text: Bacteria use sugars and starches to produce acids that remove minerals from tooth enamel. Repeated acid attacks can eventually create a cavity.

title: Tooth decay
text: Early decay can appear as a white spot. Saliva minerals and fluoride can help repair enamel before a cavity forms. A formed cavity is permanent damage.

title: Tooth decay
text: Early decay may have no symptoms. Advanced decay may cause sensitivity or toothache. Infection can cause an abscess with swelling and fever.

title: Tooth decay
text: A dentist can restore a cavity with a filling. More serious tooth damage may require a crown, root canal treatment, or extraction.

title: Periodontal gum disease
text: Plaque can harden into tartar. A dentist or dental hygienist must remove tartar professionally. Bacteria in plaque and tartar can inflame gums and supporting tissues.

title: Periodontal gum disease
text: Gum disease may cause red, swollen, bleeding or receding gums, persistent bad breath, loose teeth, and painful chewing.

title: Periodontal gum disease
text: Tobacco use is an important gum disease risk factor and can impair healing. Diabetes, aging, and genetic factors can also contribute.

title: Periodontal gum disease
text: Plaque-related early gum disease may improve with brushing and flossing. Periodontal disease needs professional treatment such as scaling and root planing; advanced disease may require surgery.

title: Dry mouth xerostomia
text: Saliva helps chewing and swallowing, clears food particles, and supplies minerals that protect teeth. Persistent dry mouth increases tooth decay and oral fungal infection risk.

title: Dry mouth xerostomia
text: Medicines, including some drugs for blood pressure and depression, can reduce saliva. Diabetes, Sjogren's disease, and cancer treatments can also cause dry mouth.

title: Dry mouth xerostomia
text: Dry mouth symptoms include a sticky mouth, difficulty chewing or swallowing, a dry throat, cracked lips, mouth sores, and bad breath.

title: Dry mouth xerostomia
text: Sipping water and chewing sugarless gum may ease dry mouth. Avoid tobacco and alcohol. Discuss causes and saliva substitutes or medicines with a doctor or dentist.

title: Oral hygiene
text: Brush teeth twice daily with fluoride toothpaste. Clean between teeth regularly, aiming for once daily, and visit a dentist for checkups and professional cleaning.

title: Oral hygiene
text: Angle brush bristles toward the gumline. Use gentle small circular motions, clean every side of each tooth, and replace the brush when its bristles wear out.

title: Oral hygiene
text: Ease floss between teeth without forcing it. Curve it around the tooth in a C shape and move it up and down. Interdental brushes or floss holders can help.

title: Oral hygiene
text: Teeth with fillings can still decay. Plaque near a chipped filling can cause new decay, and exposed roots following gum recession are also vulnerable.

title: Diabetes and oral health
text: Diabetes raises gum disease risk and can slow healing. Gum disease may make blood glucose harder to control; poor glucose control worsens oral health problems.

title: Diabetes and oral health
text: Diabetes can be associated with dry mouth and increased saliva glucose. These factors can contribute to thrush, a fungal infection with painful white patches.

title: Diabetes and oral health
text: Blood glucose control, twice daily brushing, regular flossing, routine dental visits, and quitting smoking help prevent diabetes-related oral problems. Tell the dentist about diabetes.

title: Diabetes and oral health
text: A dentist may treat periodontal disease with deep cleaning or referral to a specialist. A clinician can prescribe antifungal treatment for thrush or treatment for dry mouth.

title: Oral cancer
text: Tobacco and heavy alcohol use increase oral cancer risk; combined use increases it further. HPV infection is linked to some mouth and throat cancers.

title: Oral cancer
text: A mouth sore, red or white patch, persistent hoarseness, or trouble swallowing lasting more than two weeks should be assessed by a dentist or doctor.

title: Oral cancer
text: An oral cancer examination checks the face, neck, lips, mouth, and back of the throat. Unusual findings may require additional tests or specialist referral.

title: Oral cancer
text: Oral cancer treatment may involve surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy. Treatment choices depend on tumor features, spread, and general health.
